persona: First-time accountant reviewing a payable-control demonstration
method: Fresh browser-only review through the supplied harness. Isolation was by instruction, not an enforced technical boundary. No source, files, prior reports, live application or APIs were inspected. Only screenshots created in this review were viewed.

understanding.product: Kontor ties payment authority to a specific invoice amount, recipient and version. It requires two distinct approvals and prevents an obsolete payment instruction from spending from the program-controlled payable and vault after the invoice changes.
understanding.what_happened: Northform Studio had a 1,000 Test USD invoice approved by Mara and Jonas. Lena applied credit CN-204 for 200, making the payable 800 and expiring both old approvals. Alex attempted the saved 1,000 instruction; the tour says the program rejected its obsolete invoice version and no Test USD moved. Mara and Jonas then approved version 2 for 800, after which a recorded payment settled 800. The invoice, credit, expired approvals, rejection and settlement remain linked in the evidence history.
understanding.what_is_real: The visible interface says it reconstructs a prior run in the actual Kontor workbench. It provides Solana devnet links for recorded approval, credit, rejected payment and corrected payment transactions, and a downloadable evidence JSON. My own clicks only navigated the static replay. I did not independently verify transaction outcomes on-chain.
understanding.limits_understood: Synthetic workspace and invoice, Test USD with no monetary value, server-held demo role keys, trusted upgrade authority, unaudited prototype, and no established production custody or accounting readiness. The protection is scoped to the program-controlled payable and vault. The rejected transaction can still incur a devnet SOL fee.

actions: Viewed desktop introduction and its original-amount, credit, revised-payable and blocked-instruction summary.
Selected Follow the payment and traversed all ten snapshots across six chapters.
Used Tab and Enter to advance through the approval, credit, rejection, reapproval and payment journey. Observed a clear visible focus outline on the primary action.
Read the payment review dialog, dismissed it using Escape, reopened it using Inspect recorded payment review, and displayed the recorded result.
Read the final evidence chapter and all eight timeline events, including expired version 1 approvals and current version 2 approvals.
Clicked Download evidence JSON; harness download result reported filename recorded-evidence.json and failure null. Download contents were not read.
Changed to mobile 390x844 and visually reviewed the evidence page, payment review dialog and introduction.
Used mobile chapter navigation to revisit Pay, dismissed the dialog with Escape, used Back to return to snapshot 7, then used tour home and the direct Inspect recorded evidence entry point.

understand_problem_and_control.reason: The 1,000 minus 200 equals 800 story and the reason old approvals expire are explicit, repeated consistently in the narrative and workbench.

journey_and_navigation.reason: Specific next-action labels, chapter navigation, snapshot counts, Back and home controls made the full sequence easy to follow and revisit. The direct evidence entry point also worked.

distinguish_replay_real_outcomes_and_lim.reason: Static replay and no-transaction labels are prominent at entry, during navigation and in the payment dialog. Recorded devnet claims are separated from synthetic business data, with explicit prototype and custody limitations.

evidence_understanding.reason: The final chapter separates rejected instruction, corrected settlement and downloadable record, while the timeline preserves amount, invoice version, actor and outcome. I can explain what each evidence route is meant to substantiate; this score does not certify the underlying chain claims.

responsive_and_keyboard_clarity.reason: Mobile reflow keeps the main story and controls legible, moves the payment review ahead of detail, and provides a usable dialog. Tab/Enter progression and Escape worked. One small mobile typography collision makes the recorded control result label run directly into its title, and the long evidence page requires substantial scrolling.

findings.observation: On the 390px screenshot, the uppercase RECORDED CONTROL RESULT label runs immediately into Earlier payment attempt blocked on the same text line, weakening their separation.
findings.impact: Minor scanning friction; the explanatory paragraph and outcome remain understandable.
findings.suggestion: Put the result label and outcome title on distinct lines or provide clear spacing.

findings.observation: The complete evidence page is approximately 4,469px tall at a 390px width. The top evidence cards give the essential routes before the longer workbench history.
findings.impact: The main outcome remains accessible, but reading all history and the prototype boundary requires a long scroll.
findings.suggestion: Optional polish: provide a short jump to the evidence timeline or boundary statement; no blocker observed.

verification_limits: This review evaluates visible explanation, navigation, evidence discoverability and selected responsive/keyboard behavior, not security or accounting correctness.
Did not open external explorer transactions or audit chain data; recorded outcomes remain attributed to the visible tour.
The successful download event was checked, but JSON contents were not inspected.
No screen-reader session, exhaustive keyboard audit, color-contrast measurement or device lab testing was performed.
Duplicate top and bottom next buttons were handled with keyboard navigation and were not treated as a UI defect.
